title: Host Metrics
description: Host capacity, utilization, saturation, I/O, and optional container and Kubernetes component metrics collected by the startechnica/grafana host_metrics module. Select a group before choosing hosts: the group can be a discovered cluster or Standalone / ungrouped for hosts without a cluster_name label. Every host is still selected by its instance label, so topology labels remain optional.

list.name: group
list.label: Group
list.description: Select a cluster, or Standalone / ungrouped to list hosts without a cluster_name label.

panels.title: Hosts reporting
panels.description: Nodes that currently expose the unix exporter metric set selected above.

panels.title: Average CPU usage
panels.description: Fleet average across selected hosts. The per-host CPU view is below.

panels.title: Average memory usage
panels.description: Memory in use excluding reclaimable filesystem cache when MemAvailable is provided by the host kernel.

panels.title: Highest filesystem usage
panels.description: Highest usage among selected persistent filesystems. Pseudo filesystems and container-specific mounts are excluded by the Alloy module before collection.

panels.title: CPU pressure
panels.description: Average percentage of time tasks were delayed waiting for CPU over the selected rate interval.

panels.title: Unix scrape health
panels.description: Fraction of the selected unix exporter targets whose latest scrape succeeded.

panels.title: CPU utilization by host
panels.description: Non-idle CPU time as a percentage of all logical CPU time. A sustained value near 100% means the node has little CPU headroom.

targets.expr: 100 * sum by (instance) (rate(node_cpu_seconds_total{job="integrations/unix", mode!="idle", instance=~"${node:regex}"}[$__rate_interval])) / count by (instance) (node_cpu_seconds_total{job="integrations/unix", mode="idle", instance=~"${node:regex}"})

panels.title: Load average per CPU
panels.description: Load averages normalized by logical CPU count. Values above 1 indicate more runnable or uninterruptible work than available CPU capacity; high I/O wait can also raise load.

targets.expr: node_load1{job="integrations/unix", instance=~"${node:regex}"} / count without (cpu, mode) (node_cpu_seconds_total{job="integrations/unix", instance=~"${node:regex}"})
node_load5{job="integrations/unix", instance=~"${node:regex}"} / count without (cpu, mode) (node_cpu_seconds_total{job="integrations/unix", instance=~"${node:regex}"})
node_load15{job="integrations/unix", instance=~"${node:regex}"} / count without (cpu, mode) (node_cpu_seconds_total{job="integrations/unix", instance=~"${node:regex}"})

panels.title: CPU modes
panels.description: Aggregate CPU time by mode. Use it to distinguish computational saturation from I/O wait, guest workload, or steal time.

panels.title: CPU and I/O pressure
panels.description: Linux PSI: the percentage of elapsed time that at least one task was stalled waiting for CPU or I/O. Requires kernels that expose pressure stall information; no data on older hosts is expected.

panels.title: Memory utilization by host
panels.description: Used memory based on MemTotal minus MemAvailable. Unlike cache-inclusive gauges, this is a better signal of actual memory pressure.

panels.title: Memory available and swap used
panels.description: Available RAM and swap consumption by host. Swap use alone is not necessarily a fault; rising use with low available RAM is the meaningful combination.

panels.title: Filesystem usage
panels.description: Current use of every selected persistent filesystem. The module filters pseudo filesystems, runtime mounts, and Docker, Podman, containerd, and kubelet mounts before they become series.

panels.title: Network throughput
panels.description: Receive and transmit throughput per host and interface. Loopback and virtual interfaces remain available, so use the legend to focus on physical interfaces where necessary.

panels.title: Disk throughput
panels.description: Read and write throughput per selected block device. Select a device above to reduce visual noise on hosts with many volumes.

panels.title: Disk IOPS
panels.description: Completed read and write operations per second for the selected block devices.

panels.title: Disk busy time
panels.description: Fraction of elapsed time each block device reported itself busy. Sustained values near 100% indicate a saturated device, though virtualized storage can report this imperfectly.

panels.title: Top direct-host containers by CPU
panels.description: Only populated when the optional host_metrics.containers declare runs. It tracks direct Docker and Podman cgroups with job=integrations/cadvisor, not Kubernetes workload containers collected from the kubelet endpoint.

targets.expr: topk(10, 100 * sum by (instance, name, container_id, runtime) (rate(container_cpu_usage_seconds_total{job="integrations/cadvisor", instance=~"${node:regex}", container_id=~".+"}[$__rate_interval])))

panels.title: Top direct-host containers by memory
panels.description: Working-set memory for direct Docker and Podman cgroups. Podman containers without a Quadlet unit may not have a name label; their short container ID remains available.

targets.expr: topk(10, sum by (instance, name, container_id, runtime) (container_memory_working_set_bytes{job="integrations/cadvisor", instance=~"${node:regex}", container_id=~".+"}))

panels.title: Kubelet targets up
panels.description: Healthy kubelet scrape targets. The host_metrics.kubelet declare produces the kubelet job and explicitly stamps metrics_path labels for its four endpoints.

panels.title: Kubelet running pods
panels.description: Current number of pods reported by the local kubelet /metrics endpoint. This panel is blank when host_metrics.kubelet is not instantiated.

panels.title: Control-plane targets up
panels.description: Healthy kube-controller-manager and kube-scheduler targets. The host_metrics.control_plane declare yields no targets on workers, so this intentionally remains blank outside control-plane nodes.

panels.title: Kubelet pod count by node
panels.description: Per-node running-pod count from the optional kubelet scrape. Kubernetes workload resource dashboards should remain the source for workload-level diagnosis.

panels.title: Kubernetes scrape health
panels.description: Successful scrape fraction per optional Kubernetes component. An absent series means that declare is not enabled or the selected hosts are not control-plane nodes.
